facts.text: The palace was built in the 19th century as a private residence.
facts.excerpt: Built in the 19th century as a private residence, this palace combines classic charm and contemporary elegance

facts.text: The hotel overlooks the Tagus River.
facts.excerpt: Built in the 19th century, overlooking the Tagus River

facts.text: The palace sits atop one of Lisbon's seven hills.
facts.excerpt: Built in the 19th century, this luxurious palace sits atop one of Lisbon's seven hills overlooking the Tagus River

facts.text: The hotel is surrounded by subtropical gardens.
facts.excerpt: Surrounded by lush subtropical gardens and with a breathtaking view over the Tagus River, the Lapa Palace is a true oasis in the city center.

facts.text: The hotel is a five-star member of The Leading Hotels of the World.
facts.excerpt: As a member of "The Leading Hotels of the World", and as a five-star hotel, we celebrate the best of Portugal

facts.text: The rooms have different decorative styles: art deco, colonial, Algarve and neoclassical.
facts.excerpt: All the rooms and the suite have different styles: art deco, colonial, Algarve and neoclassical.

facts.text: The hotel has a Palace Wing and a Garden Wing.
facts.excerpt: The hotel now has two distinct wings, the Palace Wing and the Garden Wing, with a total of 95 rooms.

facts.text: Rooms in the former palace are individually decorated, and some have garden or city and river views.
facts.excerpt: Located in the former palace, the rooms are individually decorated and some have garden or city/river views.

facts.text: Le Pavillon hosts barbecues every Thursday through the summer.
facts.excerpt: Enjoy the traditional Le Pavillon Barbecues every thursdays throughout the summer

facts.text: The hotel's address is Rua do Pau de Bandeira, 4, in Lisbon.
facts.excerpt: Rua do Pau de Bandeira, 4

facts.text: The garden has fountains, fish ponds and an outdoor pool.
facts.excerpt: The jungle-y backyard is adorned with fountains, fish ponds, and a stellar outdoor pool.

facts.text: The hotel offers babysitting services and has a kids' pool.
facts.excerpt: This is also a rare family-friendly hotel with babysitting services and a kids' pool.

facts.text: Lapa Restaurant serves Mediterranean fare.
facts.excerpt: Lapa Restaurant serves Mediterranean fare in an elegant atmosphere

facts.text: The Rio Tejo Bar offers afternoon tea from May through September.
facts.excerpt: the Rio Tejo Bar offers a renowned afternoon tea service (May through September)

facts.text: Portraits of the manor's former occupants hang throughout the hotel.
facts.excerpt: portraits of the manor’s former occupants hanging throughout keep an eye on them.

facts.text: Bathrooms are marble and stocked with L'Occitane products.
facts.excerpt: marble bathrooms stocked with L'Occitane products

facts.text: Navigating the grounds can be disorienting, so guests can ask for a map at check-in.
facts.excerpt: Navigating the grounds can be a bit disorienting, so ask for a map at check-in.

facts.text: The hotel is in one of Lisbon's most historic neighborhoods.
facts.excerpt: offering an exclusive experience in one of the city’s most historic neighborhoods

facts.text: Le Pavillon serves canapes and drinks poolside.
facts.excerpt: Le Pavillion serves canapés and drinks poolside.

facts.text: Conde Nast Traveler describes the location as Lisbon's outskirts, while the official site says the heart of Lisbon.
facts.excerpt: Its location, on Lisbon’s outskirts, makes it inconvenient for those looking to stay central

contradictions.note: Official p1 says two wings (Palace and Garden) with 95 rooms; CNT p3 says 109 rooms in three wings including Villa Lapa

sources.excerpt: The hotel now has two distinct wings, the Palace Wing and the Garden Wing, with a total of 95 rooms.
The 109 rooms are divided into three wings—the Garden Wing, Palace Wing, and the independent (and posh) Villa Lapa.
